dict.string: LaVoix needs Accessibility permission to listen for global hotkeys and type text into other apps when you stop recording.
LaVoix needs microphone access to record your voice for speech-to-text transcription. Your audio is processed locally and never sent to external servers.
LaVoix needs system audio access to record the meeting application you explicitly select. Meeting audio stays on this Mac.
LaVoix needs Screen & System Audio access to record audio from the meeting application you explicitly select.
LaVoix needs permission to manage launch at startup, and to send the replies you type in the notch through the Messages app.
LaVoix uses your contacts to show names instead of phone numbers in the notch's Messages widget. Contacts stay on this Mac.
LaVoix shows your next meeting in the notch and can offer to record it when it starts. Events are read on this Mac and never leave it.
LaVoix uses on-device speech recognition to transcribe your voice commands and text quickly and privately.
